children: Anteris reported one-year outcomes for DurAVR in 100 patients with small aortic annuli: 1% had heart failure hospitalization, mean pressure gradient was 8.9 mmHg, and no valve-related mortality or moderate or severe paravalvular leak was reported.

AI Analyst View
Heart failure hospitalization: 1% at 1 year
The release cites 4.1% and 3.5% rates in the SMART trial; cross-trial comparisons are cautioned.
Mean pressure gradient: 8.9 mmHg at 1 year
Single-digit gradients are relevant to performance in small annuli; no prior-period comparison was provided.
No valve-related mortality reported at 1 year
A safety outcome in a pooled 100-patient cohort; the release provides no comparative control group.
No moderate or severe PVL observed at 1 year
A valve-performance finding, but the release provides no direct comparison with other valves.
97% free of moderate or severe PPM at 30 days
Relevant to small-annulus patients; this is a 30-day result, not a one-year measure.
PARADIGM is enrolling; plans ~1,000 patients
The randomized head-to-head pivotal trial is the next test; enrollment is planned, not completed.

These pooled early and feasibility-study results are an interim clinical data point for Anteris's investigational DurAVR valve ahead of its pivotal trial. The larger catalyst is PARADIGM's randomized comparison with commercial valves, including its one-year primary endpoint results.
